props.text: Introduction to healthcare system Dr/ Hoda Khalifa Professor of Histology and cell biology Vice dean of students’ affairs Transfer Goal Be oriented with the healthcare system and his future role as a physician. What do you want to know about health& the healthcare system in Egypt? Hospitals of Health Insurance- Military Hospitals 1ry, 2ry & 3ry healthcare Ambulatory- stationary Hospitals of Ministry Of Health& High Education Health- disease Outpatient- inpatient Governmental - private MS or MD Egyptian Fellowship, Arab Board Of Doctors& others Students’ learning outcomes At the end of this lecture the student will be able to: Discuss health dimensions Classify the health care services according to level, site, patients’ stay, rapidity and finance Identify his road to be specialist Outline What is health and its dimensions? What are the levels of health care What are the elements of primary health care? How to be a specialist? What is inpatient and outpatient medical services? How can the patient choose a hospital? Do you know such terms? Health promotion: The process of enabling people to increase control over, and to improve, their health. Health education: One of the measure of health promotion directed towards personal hygiene, nutrition, life style adopted by individual/ group of people by him self or themselves Health counselling: Any assistance to an individual seeking to solve any health problem Dimensions of Health Health care services Level Financial Site Rapidity stay payment Fund 3ry Inpatient Outpatient Medical center Hospital 2ry 1ry Center of Excellence Polyclinic Clinic Governmental private Ministry of Health High education Interior and Defense Urgent Emergency Rapid Semi- elective Elective Levels of Healthcare Primary care General practitioner Secondary care is the care of a specialist. Tertiary care is a higher level of specialized care within a hospital. Primary Healthcare: The primary focus is on the basic healthcare services that address the health issues faced by an individual. The care is mostly provided by a general physician, and they do not require a specialist Needs: Illness: When you notice a new symptom or infection. Injury: acute medical problem. Referral: to specialists and other levels of care. Who can offer this service? Doctors. Nurse practitioners Physician assistants Nutrition vaccination Maternal & child health Infectious disease prevention & treatment Endemic disease treatment Drug availability Health education & counselling Elements of Primary health care Providers Secondary Healthcare: Specialists The providers act as a channel of communication for a better advanced medical care. Specialists focus either on a specific system of the body or a particular disease as: Cardiologists focus on the heart and blood vessels. Endocrinologists focus on hormone systems, including diseases like diabetes and thyroid disease. Oncologists specialize in treating cancers, and many focus on a specific type of cancer. Tertiary Care and Hospitalization It requires highly specialized equipment and expertise as advanced diagnostic centers, specialized intensive care units and modern medical. It is the site for specialized procedures such as: Coronary artery bypass surgery Plastic & Neurosurgeries Severe burn treatments Complex treatments or procedures 17 Who can provide the service? Earning Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery , MBBCH (GP: General Practitioner) Completing training & earning Licensing Residency& advances studies Earning advanced certification (Specialist) How to Become a specialist in Egypt? Egyptian Fellowship MCCQE. Earning Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery , MBBCH (GP: General Practitioner) Completing training & earning Licensing Residency& advances studies Earning advanced certification (Specialist) MS& MD Arab Board of Medical Specializations USMLE PLAB Patients’ stay What is outpatient care? The patient don’t have to stay in a hospital. Outpatient care may be provided in a hospital, as well as a walk-in clinic, an outpatient surgery center, and even the doctor’s office. 22 What are the types of outpatient care? Medical screenings such as mammogram, colonoscopy, and endoscopy Minor surgeries and procedures that don’t require advanced medical care, such as laser surgery, hand or foot surgery, mole removal, and Lasik eye surgery Certain types of treatment used for ongoing or long-term illnesses, such as dialysis and chemotherapy What is inpatient care? provided in a hospital or other type of inpatient facility, where the patient is admitted, and spend at least one night—or more—depending on his condition. The patient is under the care of doctors, nurses, and other types of health care professionals within a hospital. Inpatient stay may be planned or unplanned. What are the examples of inpatient care? props.text: CHEMICAL BLOCKS OF LIFE: LIPIDS By Dr Sara Assem Lecturer of Medical Biochemistry & Molecular Biology DEAR STUDENTS & TRANSFER GOAL Understand the nature and importance of lipids as main nutrients and building block. STUDENTS’ LEARNING OUTCOMES(SLOs) At the end of this session, the student will be able to: Describe how lipids help us function and survive Describe the building blocks of lipids Discuss lipids’ role in health and disease Antibodies Lipids WHAT ARE LIPIDS? Heterogeneous organic compounds related to fatty acids. They contain C, H, and O and may also contain P, N, and S. Lipids are relatively insoluble in water, and soluble in in nonpolar solvents (fat solvents) as ether, benzene and acetone. Derived Lipids Complex Lipids Simple Lipids CLASSIFICATION OF LIPIDS Monoacylglycerol True Lipids Di-acyl-glycerol Tri-acyl-glycerol Waxes 1st Fatty Acid 2nd Fatty Acid 3rd Fatty Acid FATTY ACIDS AND ALCOHOLS TOGETHER WITH SOME OTHER HEAD Phospholipids Glycolipids Derived Lipids PROPERTIES OF FATTY ACIDS Hydrophobic Hydrophilic However, for long chain length fatty acids , the hydrophobic portion is predominant. These molecules are highly water insoluble and must be transported in the circulation in association with protein. 1- Amphipathic 2- FATTY ACID SATURATION In general, addition of double bonds decreases the melting temperature (Tm) of a fatty acid, whereas increasing the chain length increases the Tm In humans, the majority are saturated or monounsaturated. 3 carbons apart 2- FATTY ACID SATURATION In general, addition of double bonds decreases the melting temperature (Tm) of a fatty acid, whereas increasing the chain length increases the Tm Cis Bonds Trans Bonds functional group on the same side functional group on opposite sides 3- FATTY ACID CHAIN LENGTH Short Chain FA 2-6 carbons Medium Chain FA 7-12 carbons Long Chain FA >12 Play role in intestinal health They are now gaining popularity as a healthy diet component and as a dietary supplement where it contains fewer calories and gives higher satiety . Moreover, they improve gut health by killing harmful bacteria without impacting good bacteria, preventing diarrhea and bloating. They are the greatest bulk of FA in animal tissues and most animal diets. In the human body, fatty acids with an even number of carbon atoms (16, 18, or 20) predominate. Longer fatty acids (>22 carbons) being found in the brain. 4-RANCIDITY Slight hydrolysis of fat leading to liberation of short chain FA volatile having bad odour Oxidation of the unsaturated fatty acids occurs with the formation of peroxides, aldehydes and ketones RANCIDITY Can be inhibited by keeping fat in cold clean place away from light and moisture or addition of antioxidant like vitamins A, E. 5-FATTY ACIDS NUMBERING There are two systems of numbering the carbon atoms in a fatty acid ESSENTIAL FA THAT MUST BE PROVIDED IN DIET INCLUDE: Linoleic acid, the precursor of ω-6 fatty acids (ie: Fatty acids with the terminal double bond being six bonds from the ω end.) α-linolenic acid, the precursor of ω-3 fatty acids. (ie: Fatty acids with the terminal double bond being three bonds from the ω end.) Essential fatty acid deficiency occurs most often in infants fed diets deficient in EFAs. props.text: Basics of writing essay & reflections SLO’s At the end of this session the students will be able to Conclude the requirements for medical academic writing. Stress and its correlates among medical students in six medical colleges: an attempt to understand the current situation Abstract Background: Medical students encounter various stressors during their studies. The study aimed to assess stress levels, sources, and associated determinants among Sudanese medical students. Method: An online questionnaire-based study was conducted among 617 undergraduate medical students of 6 different universities in Sudan. A 19-item questionnaire was utilized to assess stress sources, in addition to demographics, stress manifestations, and coping strategies. Results: The overall prevalence of stress was 31.7% (p <0.05). The main sources of stress were time pressure, heavy workload, fear of failure, and examination frequency. One-third of students indicated that they experienced at least one source of psychosocial- and teaching-related stress. Female medical students were more significantly stressed due to academics than males. Also, fourth- and fifth-year students were academically more stressed in comparison to the first-year students. Poisson regression analysis model showed that first-year students were less stressed than the final-year students in relation to academics (odds=0.888, P=0.003). Male medical students, across all study years, were far less stressed than females (odds=0.901, P=0.000153). Expectedly, ‘studying medicine by choice’ was associated with decreased odds for psychosocial stressors (odds=0.885, P=0.00781), and improved model-fit (chi squared=6.8952, P=0.008643). Also, the year of study was a predictor of teaching-related stress development Conclusions: Female medical students were more stressed due to academics than males. On the other hand, final year students were more academically stressed than first-year students. Female medical students were likely having stress related to academic stress development, while being first-year medical student was a predictor of not developing academic stress. Studying medicine by choice’ was associated with ability to cope against stress. Keywords: Stress, Medical students, Medical education, Sudan It is an example of Academic writing. What in fact are the characteristics that lead us to this conclusion? What linguistic features and other characteristics in your opinion make this an example of medical academic writing? What is academic writing? Based on facts and data (research, not opinions) Sounds formal (uses an academic vocabulary) Draws on information from expert sources (references) Based on facts and data Source: research work with reference we use other people’s information, and show respect to those who wrote it It is written in a formal-sounding vocabulary (which uses academic words and avoids the personal perspective) We use other people’s information, and show respect to those who wrote it Do you really write like that? Really no one writes like this EXCEPT in academic writing When you will use academic writing? To present an assignment (poster, article or power point presentation) To share in students’ conferences To share in scientific competitions Academic writing – general rules The use of sources Quotations Vocabulary characteristic of a specific field Formal language and format Vocabulary Structures Absence of features of spoken language Layout Matter-of-fact style Style of academic writing Formal Impersonal Precise Cautious Unemotional Style of academic writing Formality This piece of writing 🡪the present study (=this study) My essay’ ll make it clear 🡪the present paper will clarify • Impersonality Many of my friends and colleagues say that… 🡪 It is commonly said that… I, you, my friend Dave 🡪 the present study/author, one, Robertson (1992) • Precision Pets like cats, dogs, etc. 🡪 pets, such as cats and dogs, Around half of the group 🡪 approximately 53% of the group Style of academic writing • Caution Our study proves that 🡪 This study shows that I’m sure this is so. 🡪 There is reason to believe that this is so. We really couldn’t make anything of the results. 🡪 There were difficulties in analysing the results. • Lack of emotion (an objective, unemotional stance) I think that this idea sucks. 🡪This idea may not be accurate. In my opinion this is a wonderful topic. 🡪This topic is worth investigating because…. Organization Make your texts well-organized: divide your text into sensible components (main sections, paragraphs subsections,.......). What is a paragraph? A paragraph is a collection of related sentences dealing with a single topic. Paragraph style Effective paragraphs = Unity, Coherence &Economy of expression Unity A topic sentence (general idea) Adequate Development (discussed fully and adequately). Cohesion (language indicates the links between the various issues Coherence (interrelated issues are presented logically) Economy of expression Did I do it well? Sorry but there is plagiarism Plagiarism is: (a) a dangerous disease (b) an academic offence (c) an academic website Plagiarism Copied writing from someone else’s work (a book, a website, another student’s essay etc) Used ideas that someone else researched or developed without referencing the original source Made mistakes with their paraphrasing and referencing (such as only putting some parts of the writing into their own words) Paraphrasing means putting ideas into your own words (but you still reference where it came from!) To avoid plagiarism, follow these steps: Take notes when reading: Always take note of where information has come from (where you read it, who wrote it) Develop your skills: Learn how to quote, paraphrase and reference properly Protect yourself: Never give your work/ assignments to another student Types of academic medical writing Essays Reports Lab report Annotated bibliography Case study What Is a Reflective Essay? Analyzing one’s experience, its meaning, and lessons can be learned from it. An experience you will never forget. The moment you overcame a fear. The most difficult choice you had to make. A time your beliefs were challenged. A time something changed your life. A time you felt lost. An introspective look at your choices A moment in your life you would like to relive. A reflective essay It is a type of writing in which you describe some moment or experience from your life or share your thoughts on some text. The experience should explore your personal ideas, feelings, and opinions about the event and how it affected you There is no right or wrong way to write reflectively! Reflective style Personal in nature: use the personal pronoun “I” Talk about your own thoughts and feelings. Not to be too casual or conversational. Include essential details, Written directly and concisely. Clear examples are very useful. Deeper level reflective writing may also connect with the literature as evidence. Howatson-Jones, L (2010). Reflecting writing. In Reflective practice in nursing. Exeter; Learning Matters p. 120-121 Take home message Academic writing: Based on facts and data (research, not opinions) Sounds formal (uses an academic vocabulary) Draws on information from expert sources (references) To avoid plagiarism learn how to quote, paraphrase and reference properly Reflective writing is personal and feelings are the core of it Reference All the pictures included in presentation were obtained from google search https://slideplayer.com/slide/12710164 Cottrell S. Skinner Has to do more with behaviors, attitudes, and emotions You “learn” to Worry less about exams Be more positive towards studying Focus more during lectures and studying Attend lectures more often أيوة سمعتك، أعمل ايه بقى؟ Phase 1: Pre-lecture prep Before the lecture Playful reading Not looking to remember, learn, or understand Just collect as much random points about the topis so you can join the conversation in the lecture Looking on random sources including non-scientific ones can be useful. This helps you ask your professor about common misconceptions and get an expert rebuttal. Phase 2: Lecture Attentive listening Not looking to remember or learn Very important to UNDERSTAND Take notes about unclear topics, incomplete answers, parts that challenged you, good mind maps, mnemonics….etc Ask a lot of questions DO NOT GO OUT OF THE LECTURE WITH ANY BLURRED POINTS You don’t have to remember everything, but you must understand as much as you can. Phase 3: Review Soon after the lecture Write your own study notes using your lecture notes, textbook, online resources, personal thoughts…etc Integrate information together Integrate with other lectures and topics Find points of concordance and conflict between different fields and topics Phase 4: Consolidation Checkpoints (commonly every 1-2 weeks) Review the material Clarify any missing points by visiting textbooks or other resources and by discussing these specific points with colleagues or professors Phase 5: Revision Immediately before exam Easiest step in studying Refresh your memory by skimming over the large bullet points Practice with questions Rephrase bullet-points into answers Time Management The art of arranging, organizing, scheduling, and budgeting one’s time " Preventing time robberies Social media Video games Computer& calls Time-robbing visitors Attending unorganized meetings Following unclear directions to any place Sleep Stay focused and Don't forget to live your life, enjoy your time and practice your hobbies Procrastination 80%–95% of college students engage in procrastination, planning fallacy, we underestimate the time required to accomplish assignments. "Student syndrome" a student will only begin to fully apply themselves to a task immediately before a deadline. Procrastination Signs: Ø often end up doing something you like to do instead of what you should do. Ø put required work out of sight so you won’t be reminded of it. Ø You tell yourself you need time to relax and rest. Ø You think you are ill Ø You manage to start late and then convince yourself that there isn’t enough time to do the task that day. Ø You conveniently forget to have needed materials at hand to do a task. The act of postponing, delaying or putting off Reactions to procrastination Avoidance& Distraction Trivialization & Denial Downward counterfactuals Humor & Reframing External attributions 22 How to Beat procrastination? 1- Stop thinking. Start doing. 2. Don’t blow a task out of proportion. 3. Just take the first step. 4. Start with the hardest task of your day. 5. Just make a decision. Any decision. 6. Face your fear. 7. Finish it. Exam taken strategies MCQ exams MCQ questions can generally be classified into questions where you: know the answer even before reading the choices need to read the choices to identify the answer will need to think between two close answers Figure out the correct answer by exclusion Without being sure, chose the answer you think makes most sense Have no idea what the right answer is You need to be wary of the effect of anxiety on your performance. Being anxious can affect your memory, attention, concentration, self-confidence, and in general can very easily move questions down several categories. Thus, a question where you could’ve identified the answer easily will suddenly (with self-doubt) become a question where you’re trying to figure the answer out by exclusion. This ends up consuming more time and propagating anxiety causing a vicious cycle and destroying performance MCQ exams MCQ exams Go through the exam answering only questions in the first two categories: know the answer even before reading the choices need to read the choices to identify the answer If you have studied well, this should cover at least 50 – 60% of the questions Next, you go through the remaining questions answering the following two categories: will need to think between two close answers Figure out the correct answer by exclusion This will cover another 20 – 30%. You have now covered 70 – 90% of the exam Finally read the remaining difficult questions from the last two categories well Without being sure, chose the answer you think makes most sense Have no idea what the right answer is At this point, not knowing the answer to these questions may frustrate you but remember you have already finished about 80% of your exam. So, you probably won’t be anxious and even if you are, it’s safe to panic now ☺ Start reading each question and doing your best at figuring the best هبدة you can come up with. If you REALLY draw a blank, then chose one fixed answer for all remaining questions. The proper technique for writing an academic essay is similar to general rules of essay writing everywhere. You have to divide your answer into Opening paragraph, where you rephrase the question and give a present the bullet-points of your answer Several paragraphs detailing key points of your answer (one point/paragraph) End your essay with a review of the points to cover and a conclusion. Presentations Same as essay structure Make use of AV aids. Leave the writing for the slides and use your narration to enrich presentation If you only read words from slides then you might as well have just sent an essay Practical exams “Practical” comes from “practice” Practice, practice, practice Then keep practicing And when done, practice some more When you stop practicing, your “practical” skills will decline If you want to know who in your class is going to get the highest score in practical exams, ask who spent most time practicing. It also helps to understand the reason behind the practice being studied but you really don’t get marks for that, and nothing beats “muscle memory” Summary Types of memories are episodic, semantic and procedural. Good preparation starts before the lecture till the exam. Time management is the art of arranging, organizing, scheduling, and budgeting one’s time. props.text: Prepared By: Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry & Molecular Biology Orientation to NMD1101 Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Dear students Welcome to NMD1101: “Cell Biology & Life Cycle” Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Basic information you need to know about the course: Code: NMD1101 Credit Hours: 6 No of weeks: 6 Marks: 150 Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology So, what is the goal of studying cell biology and life cycle?? Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology The aim of this course is to help you be acquainted with the structure and function of somatic cells and outline the germ cell division and principals of embryogenesis and fetal progression with respect to genetic outcome. All such topics will be correlated to their impact on health and disease Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology You will be acquainted with: 1- Somatic cells, including all the structures involved in its composition. In addition you will study related molecular and cell biology and their implications in health and disease Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology You will be acquainted with: 2-Germ cells, genetic and principles of embryogenesis and fetal progression with respect to genetic impact in health and disorders. Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology So, what are the basic medical sciences studied along your courses? Anatomy Physiology Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Histology and cell biology Pathology Pharmacology Microbiology/ parasitology Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology 8 So, Can we guide you step by step through this course? Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology All courses studied in the pre-clerkship phase include the following Lectures Practical PBL Tutorials Clinical skills Medical professions Research PBL Lectures Practical 3 41 41 Lectures 11 Practical 3 PBL 6 weeks Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology 10 Cell biology block Important Tips Watch the lectures videos on the youtube channel rather than the portal window. This can allow you to speed up or slow down. You can also turn CAPTIONS ON. Don’t forget to self-correct your activity sheets during face to face sessions Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology Lectures Lectures will be given in hallrooms, with an average of 2 lectures/day. All lectures are given face to face in addition to being recorded on your portal. Practical sessions In the lab Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology In the hall rooms (tutorials) Problem I: The birth of a new drug Problem II: What is Happening to Mr Ahmed? Problem III: Lara’s agony during pregnancy PBL Week 1-6 Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology So, How will I study?? Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology First, check your schedule on daily and weekly basis On the schedule you have on the students’ hub, You will know which lectures you are supposed to prepare for the week You can take advantage of your long weekend to watch these lectures Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology During watching the lectures videos, take notes After the watching the lecture, solve the related activity sheet You can read the PDF before or after watching the lecture If you have any questions after studying, please post them on the discussion forum Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology On your schedule, you will have all lectures “Face To Face”, In face to face sessions, the time will be available for discussions& revising the activity sheets. Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology On your schedule, you also have sessions called “Practical” These practical sessions are intended to be taken in the lab… MAKE SURE YOU HAVE YOUR LAB COATS WITH YOU! In each lecture, the information you are introduced to will be correlated to different health disorders and/or drugs used to modify the condition Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology ASSESSMENT Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology Dr. Yasmine Amr Issa- Associate Professor of Medical Biochemistry andMolecular Biology Assessment Method Weight in marks Periodicity Date Summative Assessment Continuous assessment (week) (30%) 37 Every 2 weeks Cont. assessment 1 MCQs : 4-11-2023 (20 marks) Cont. assessment 2 (short answers): 18-11-2023 (17 marks) Assignment (10%) 15 Once 27-11-2023 Final written (40%) 60 Once 3-12-2023 Practical (20 %) 30 Once 7-12-2023 PBL 8 Assessed along PBL sessions TOTAL MARKS: 150 Formative Assessment In all tutorial and practical classes - Weekly Mock electronic exam - Before each written assessment Mock practical and assignment - Once 25-11-2023 24 The academy teaches through integration.
